Svencionys Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vilniaus apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Svencionys produced an extraordinary concentration of significant Jewish figures: Isaac Jacob Reines, the town's own native son who founded the Mizrachi Religious Zionist movement (and who later served as rabbi in Saukenai, documented elsewhere in this collection); Arkadi Kremer, known as the 'Father of the Bund'; Mordecai Kaplan, founder of Reconstructionist Judaism; and Yitzhak Arad, the Israeli historian who directed Yad Vashem from 1972 to 1993. The town's spiritual life centered on the 'Shulhoyf,' a courtyard of three synagogues, and several yeshivas, the most famous founded by Reines himself. In September 1941, Svencionys's Jews, together with those of Svencioneliai, documented elsewhere in this collection, were relocated to former Soviet military barracks; around 8,000 were executed there beginning October 8. This cemetery, one of the oldest in Lithuania, dating to the 17th century, had some of its tombstones used for construction by the German occupation army itself in 1941; a separate massacre of 40 Svencionys men took place directly on the cemetery grounds on May 20, 1942.
